q: What actually creates the price spike when a major US release comes out?
opts: The surprise: how far the actual lands from the forecast
why: The forecast is already priced in. Only the gap between actual and forecast — the surprise — creates the spike.

q: Which measure does the Fed officially target at 2%?
why: The Fed's policy target is 2% Core PCE YoY — Core PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge.

q: When is the NFP (Non-Farm Payrolls) report released each month?
opts: First Friday of each month, 08:30 ET
why: NFP comes out on the first Friday of every month at 08:30 ET — jobs, unemployment and wages together.

q: CPI comes in hotter than expected. What is the typical market reaction?
why: Hotter-than-expected inflation is hawkish — it pushes the Fed toward hikes, lifting USD and yields while weighing on gold.

q: Inflation is falling toward 2% and the job market is weakening. The Fed is most likely to…
opts: Cut rates — USD down, gold up (dovish)
why: Cooling inflation and weak jobs open the door to cuts (dovish), which usually pushes USD down and gold up.
